newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says Clinton win good for stability.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says Clinton win good for stability.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday congratulated U.S. President Bill Clinton for his "brilliant" re-election victory, saying it was a welcome sign of stability in an unstable world.

Prodi, leader of a centre-left coalition, sent a message to Clinton in which he congratulated the Democrat "for your brilliant reconfirmation of highest responsibility as President of the United States...," a statement from Prodi's office said.
"Your leadership will continue to constitute a factor of stability and safety in a world troubled by uncertainty, unrest and anxiety," Prodi said.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, in a radio interview, said Clinton's victory would mean continuity at home and abroad.
"I don't expect great changes...even though he will make some changes in his government," Dini said. "The political lines regarding both the economy and foreign policy will likely remain unchanged."
Italian newspapers trumpeted Clinton's victory in banner headlines and pages and pages of coverage.
"Clinton President into the Year 2000," the respected La Stampa newspaper declared.
The left-leaning La Repubblica newspaper said in a front-page editorial that the victory had secured a "Clinton Era".

"Two consecutive victories, the maximum permitted by the Constitution, establishes a historic era like the "Roosevelt Era' and the "Reagan Era'...," La Repubblica said. "The American century will end with the mark of William Jefferson Clinton."
